products.title: Quectel 4G Communication Module EG800Z
products.body_html:
Quectel EG800Z-CN (EG800ZCN10LA) — What You Need To Know Before You Buy

We have sample units of the Quectel EG800Z LTE Cat 1 bis module. These are the China regional variant (-CN), not the European variant (-EU) that is the normal choice for Nigeria. The chip is identical. The radio front-end is not. Here is exactly what that changes.

What it supports

Bands
LTE-FDD B1 (2100), B3 (1800), B5 (850), B8 (900)
LTE-TDD B34, B38, B39, B40 (2300), B41
2G / GSM None

Max 10 Mbps down / 5 Mbps up. Single antenna. LGA, 17.7 × 15.8 mm.

What this means on Nigerian networks

Works:

  • Airtel and 9mobile — both run LTE on B3 (1800 MHz). Full normal service.
  • MTN — works on its B3 (1800 MHz) layer, which is widely deployed in Lagos, Abuja and other major cities.
  • Spectranet / SWIFT — B40 (2300 MHz) is supported.

Does not work:

  • MTN B20 (800 MHz) — this is MTN's deep-coverage layer. It is what carries signal indoors, in dense buildings, and outside the cities. This module cannot see it.
  • Glo B28 (700 MHz) — Glo's main LTE coverage band. Not supported. Glo will be unreliable.
  • B7 (2600 MHz) — MTN and Glo capacity band. Not supported.

No 2G fallback. If LTE drops out at your site, the module goes offline. It will not fall back to GSM/GPRS the way many older M2M modules do.

Buy these if

  • Your device sits in Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt or another major city
  • You are on an Airtel or 9mobile SIM, or MTN in a confirmed-1800 area
  • It is a fixed installation where you can test signal once and leave it
  • You are prototyping, developing firmware, or building a demo unit — the AT command set, drivers and QuecOpen SDK are identical to the EU variant, so anything you build here ports straight over

Do not buy these if

  • You are deploying outside major cities or across mixed/unknown locations
  • Your fleet uses MTN or Glo SIMs and depends on rural or in-building coverage
  • You need 2G fallback for reliability
  • You are shipping a commercial product to NCC type approval — these carry Chinese certification (SRRC/CCC), not CE/RED, which makes the approval paperwork harder

Our recommendation

For development, prototyping and urban fixed installs, these are the same module and we're happy to sell them to you.

For production fleets going out across Nigeria, buy the EG800Z-EU instead. It adds B7, B20 and B28 and covers every LTE band any Nigerian operator runs. We can source it — talk to us and we'll quote it.

This part is being replaced in our line by the EG915U-EU, which adds 2G fallback on top of full Nigerian band coverage. Once current stock is gone, that is what we will carry.

products.title: SN74LS112N Logic Gates IC
products.body_html:
What it is

The SN74LS112N has two independent J-K flip-flops in a 16-pin DIP. Each has its own clock, J and K inputs, Q and Q outputs, and active-LOW preset and clear inputs. Outputs change on the falling edge of the clock. The inputs are fully buffered, so the flip-flop never loads the signals driving it.

It has the same logic as the older 74LS76, but with the standard power pinout (VCC pin 16, GND pin 8). That makes it the easiest dual J-K flip-flop to use on a breadboard or PCB.

Function table (each flip-flop)

PRE CLR CLK J K Q Q Mode
L H X X X H L Preset (async set)
H L X X X L H Clear (async reset)
L L X X X H* H* Not allowed (unstable)
H H ↓ L L Q0 Q0 Hold
H H ↓ H L H L Set
H H ↓ L H L H Reset
H H ↓ H H Q0 Q0 Toggle
H H H X X Q0 Q0 No change

↓ = falling (HIGH-to-LOW) clock edge. X = don't care. Q0 = previous state. *Pulling PRE and CLR LOW together forces both outputs HIGH, and the final state is unpredictable when they are released. Avoid it.

Pinout (DIP-16, top view, notch at the top)

Pin Signal Function Pin Signal Function
1 1CLK FF1 clock (falling edge) 16 VCC +5 V supply
2 1K FF1 K input 15 1CLR FF1 clear, active-LOW
3 1J FF1 J input 14 2CLR FF2 clear, active-LOW
4 1PRE FF1 preset, active-LOW 13 2CLK FF2 clock (falling edge)
5 1Q FF1 output 12 2K FF2 K input
6 1Q FF1 inverted output 11 2J FF2 J input
7 2Q FF2 inverted output 10 2PRE FF2 preset, active-LOW
8 GND Ground 9 2Q FF2 output

Specifications

Parameter Value
Logic family 74LS (low-power Schottky TTL)
Function Two independent J-K flip-flops, negative-edge-triggered, with preset and clear
Package DIP-16 (PDIP, through-hole)
Supply voltage (VCC) 4.75 V min / 5 V nom / 5.25 V max
Absolute max supply / input voltage 7 V
Input HIGH threshold (VIH) 2.0 V min
Input LOW threshold (VIL) 0.8 V max
Output HIGH voltage (VOH) 2.7 V min / 3.4 V typ at −0.4 mA
Output LOW voltage (VOL) 0.35 V typ / 0.5 V max at 8 mA
Output current −0.4 mA source (HIGH) / 8 mA sink (LOW)
Clock frequency 0–30 MHz guaranteed (fmax 30 MHz min, 45 MHz typ)
Propagation delay (clock / async input → Q, Q) 15 ns typ / 20 ns max (2 kΩ, 15 pF)
Setup time (J, K before clock ↓) 20 ns (data) · 25 ns (CLR inactive) · 20 ns (PRE inactive)
Hold time (after clock ↓) 0 ns
Minimum pulse width CLK HIGH 20 ns · PRE / CLR LOW 25 ns
Supply current (whole chip) 4 mA typ / 6 mA max
Input current (LOW) J, K: −0.4 mA max · PRE, CLR, CLK: −0.8 mA max
Operating temperature 0 °C to 70 °C

Using flip-flops

  • Tie CLR and PRE HIGH for normal operation. They are active-LOW. If one floats or is pulled LOW, it overrides the clock and the flip-flop looks "stuck". This is the most common reason these chips seem dead.
  • Debounce switches before they reach CLK. A mechanical push-button bounces and produces several clock edges per press, so a toggle circuit appears to skip. Use an RC filter plus a Schmitt trigger (74LS14) or an SR latch built from two 74LS00 gates.
  • Divide-by-2 / toggle: tie J and K HIGH. Q flips on every falling clock edge, so Q runs at half the clock frequency.
  • Ripple counter: with J = K = HIGH, feed flip-flop 1's Q into flip-flop 2's CLK to get a 2-bit binary counter (÷4). Chain more chips for more bits.

Wiring it up

  • 5 V only. 74LS is TTL logic and needs 4.75–5.25 V on VCC. It will not run reliably from 3.3 V.
  • Decouple it. Put a 100 nF ceramic capacitor between VCC and GND, as close to the chip as you can.
  • Don't leave inputs floating. An open TTL input usually reads HIGH, but it picks up noise and gives random glitches. Tie unused inputs to VCC (directly or through 1 kΩ) or to GND.
  • Arduino Uno / Nano / Mega (5 V): connect directly, no level shifting needed.
  • ESP32, Raspberry Pi, STM32 and other 3.3 V boards: a 3.3 V output driving a 74LS input is fine (HIGH threshold is 2.0 V). The other direction is not: a 74LS output can sit around 3.4–3.6 V when HIGH, which is above what 3.3 V-only pins accept. Use a divider (1 kΩ in series, 2 kΩ to GND) or a level shifter, or use the 74HC/74HCT version of the chip instead.
  • Driving LEDs: 74LS outputs sink current (8 mA) much better than they source it (0.4 mA). Wire the LED and a 680 Ω–1 kΩ resistor from +5 V to the output, so the LED lights when the output is LOW.

In the package

1 × SN74LS112N in a 16-pin plastic DIP (through-hole, 2.54 mm pin pitch, 7.62 mm / 0.3" row spacing). It drops straight into a breadboard across the centre channel. For soldered builds, use a DIP socket so the chip can be swapped.

The markings depend on the batch: you may get Texas Instruments (SN74LS…N), Hitachi/Renesas (HD74LS…P) or another second-source maker. They are all the same standard 74LS part: same pinout, same logic, same 5 V ratings.

Which J-K flip-flop do I need?

  • SN74LS73N: clear only, 14 pins, power on pins 4 and 11.
  • SN74LS76N: preset and clear, 16 pins, power on pins 5 and 13 (older part).
  • SN74LS112N (this chip): preset and clear, 16 pins, standard corner power. Recommended for new builds.

products.body_html:
What it is

The SN74LS00N has four independent 2-input NAND gates in a 14-pin DIP. NAND is the "universal" gate: NOT, AND, OR, XOR and simple memory latches can all be built from NAND gates alone. That is why the 74LS00 is the first chip in almost every digital-electronics course and lab kit.

Truth table (each gate)

A B Y
L L H
L H H
H L H
H H L

The output goes LOW only when both inputs are HIGH.

Pinout (DIP-14, top view, notch at the top)

Pin Signal Function Pin Signal Function
1 1A Gate 1 input 14 VCC +5 V supply
2 1B Gate 1 input 13 4B Gate 4 input
3 1Y Gate 1 output 12 4A Gate 4 input
4 2A Gate 2 input 11 4Y Gate 4 output
5 2B Gate 2 input 10 3B Gate 3 input
6 2Y Gate 2 output 9 3A Gate 3 input
7 GND Ground 8 3Y Gate 3 output

GND is pin 7 and VCC is pin 14. This is the standard power arrangement for 14-pin 74-series gates.

Specifications

Parameter Value
Logic family 74LS (low-power Schottky TTL)
Function Four independent 2-input NAND gates, Y = NOT(A · B)
Package DIP-14 (PDIP, through-hole)
Supply voltage (VCC) 4.75 V min / 5 V nom / 5.25 V max
Absolute max supply / input voltage 7 V
Input HIGH threshold (VIH) 2.0 V min
Input LOW threshold (VIL) 0.8 V max

Output LOW voltage (VOL) 0.35 V typ / 0.5 V max at 8 mA
Output current −0.4 mA source (HIGH) / 8 mA sink (LOW)

Handy circuits

  • Inverter (NOT): tie both inputs of one gate together.
  • AND: a NAND gate followed by a second gate wired as an inverter.
  • OR: invert each input with its own gate, then feed both into a third NAND.
  • SR latch / switch debouncer: cross-couple two gates (each output into one input of the other). Pulling one free input LOW sets the latch and the other resets it. This is the classic clean-up for a bouncy push-button.
  • Half adder: pair it with the SN74LS86N XOR gate. The sum is A XOR B and the carry is A AND B (two NAND gates).

  • ESP32, Raspberry Pi, STM32 and other 3.3 V boards: a 3.3 V output driving a 74LS input is fine (HIGH threshold is 2.0 V). The other direction is not: a 74LS output can sit around 3.4–3.6 V when HIGH, which is above what 3.3 V-only pins accept. Use a divider (1 kΩ in series, 2 kΩ to GND) or a level shifter, or use the 74HC/74HCT version of the chip instead.
  • Driving LEDs: 74LS outputs sink current (8 mA) much better than they source it (0.4 mA). Wire the LED and a 680 Ω–1 kΩ resistor from +5 V to the output, so the LED lights when the output is LOW.
  • Unused gates: tie their inputs to VCC or GND so they don't oscillate or draw extra current.

products.title: SN74LS73N IC

What it is

The SN74LS73N has two independent J-K flip-flops in a 14-pin DIP. Each has its own clock, J and K inputs, Q and Q outputs, and an active-LOW clear input. Outputs change on the falling edge of the clock. It is a 1-bit memory cell and the basic part for counters, frequency dividers and simple state machines.

⚠ Power pins are not in the corners. On this chip VCC is pin 4 and GND is pin 11. If you wire it like a 74LS00 (GND 7, VCC 14), power goes to an output and an input. Check twice before switching on.

CLR CLK J K Q Q Mode
L X X X L H Clear (async reset)
H ↓ L L Q0 Q0 Hold
H ↓ H L H L Set
H ↓ L H L H Reset
H ↓ H H Q0 Q0 Toggle
H H X X Q0 Q0 No change

↓ = falling (HIGH-to-LOW) clock edge. X = don't care. Q0 = previous state.

Pin Signal Function Pin Signal Function
1 1CLK FF1 clock (falling edge) 14 1J FF1 J input
2 1CLR FF1 clear, active-LOW 13 1Q FF1 inverted output
3 1K FF1 K input 12 1Q FF1 output
4 VCC +5 V supply 11 GND Ground
5 2CLK FF2 clock (falling edge) 10 2K FF2 K input
6 2CLR FF2 clear, active-LOW 9 2Q FF2 output
7 2J FF2 J input 8 2Q FF2 inverted output

Parameter Value

Function Two independent J-K flip-flops, negative-edge-triggered, with clear (no preset)

Using flip-flops

  • Tie CLR HIGH for normal operation. They are active-LOW. If one floats or is pulled LOW, it overrides the clock and the flip-flop looks "stuck". This is the most common reason these chips seem dead.
  • Debounce switches before they reach CLK. A mechanical push-button bounces and produces several clock edges per press, so a toggle circuit appears to skip. Use an RC filter plus a Schmitt trigger (74LS14) or an SR latch built from two 74LS00 gates.
  • Divide-by-2 / toggle: tie J and K HIGH. Q flips on every falling clock edge, so Q runs at half the clock frequency.
  • Ripple counter: with J = K = HIGH, feed flip-flop 1's Q into flip-flop 2's CLK to get a 2-bit binary counter (÷4). Chain more chips for more bits.

  • 5 V only. 74LS is TTL logic and needs 4.75–5.25 V on VCC. It will not run reliably from 3.3 V.
  • Decouple it. Put a 100 nF ceramic capacitor between VCC and GND, as close to the chip as you can.
  • Don't leave inputs floating. An open TTL input usually reads HIGH, but it picks up noise and gives random glitches. Tie unused inputs to VCC (directly or through 1 kΩ) or to GND.

What it is

The SN74LS86N has four independent 2-input exclusive-OR (XOR) gates in a 14-pin DIP. An XOR output is HIGH when its two inputs are different and LOW when they match. That makes it the building block for binary adders, parity checkers, equality comparators and switchable inverters.

  • Equality comparator: XOR each pair of bits. All outputs LOW means the two numbers are equal.

  • 5 V only. 74LS is TTL logic and needs 4.75–5.25 V on VCC. It will not run reliably from 3.3 V.
  • Decouple it. Put a 100 nF ceramic capacitor between VCC and GND, as close to the chip as you can.

Use a divider (1 kΩ in series, 2 kΩ to GND) or a level shifter, or use the 74HC/74HCT version of the chip instead.
  • Driving LEDs: 74LS outputs sink current (8 mA) much better than they source it (0.4 mA). Wire the LED and a 680 Ω–1 kΩ resistor from +5 V to the output, so the LED lights when the output is LOW.
  • Fan-out: each XOR input is two LS loads (−0.8 mA), so one 74LS output can drive up to 10 of them.

10UH Inductor

An inductor is a passive electronic component that stores energy in the form of a magnetic field. In its simplest form, an inductor consists of a wire loop or coil. The inductance is directly proportional to the number of turns in the coil. Inductors are used with capacitors in various wirelesscommunications applications. An inductor connected in series or parallel with a capacitor can provide discrimination against unwanted signals. Large inductors are used in the power supplies of electronic equipment of all types, including computers and their peripherals. In these systems, the inductors help to smooth out the rectified utility AC, providing pure, battery-like DC.

products.body_html:
Description :

An incremental encoder is a rotary sensor that converts rotational displacement into a series of digital pulse signals. These pulses are used to control angular displacement.

In the Eltra encoder, the conversion of angular displacement adopts the principle of photoelectric scanning. The reading system is based on the rotation of a radial grating (code disk) composed of alternating transparent and opaque windows. At the same time, it is illuminated by an infrared light source. The light projects the image of the code disk onto the surface of the receiver.

The receiver is covered with a grating that has the same window width as the code disk. The receiver works by sensing changes in light caused by the rotation of the disk, converting the light changes into corresponding electrical signals. The signals are then amplified to a high level and generate square-wave pulses without interference. These must be processed by electronic circuits.

The reading system usually adopts a differential method, comparing two signals with the same waveform but a 180° phase difference to improve output signal quality and stability. The reading is formed based on the difference between the two signals, thereby eliminating interference.
